script: NBA players who showed up UNRECOGNIZABLE after! At the end of the summer in 2021, Jayson Tatum posted some gym photos on his social media, and honestly, nobody was ready for them. The skinny kid the Celtics drafted out of Duke was gone, because in these pictures he looked thick, he looked strong, and he was throwing around heavy dumbbells like they were nothing. People estimated he packed on around fifteen to twenty pounds of pure muscle in one offseason, and fans immediately started saying he was bulking up the exact same way Giannis Antetokounmpo did before he turned into a monster. But the reason he did this had nothing to do with the photos. See, up to this point, Tatum won games with his length and his smooth jumper instead of brute force, and that was actually costing him. The year before he averaged 26.4 points a game, which is elite, yet he only got to the free throw line about five times a night. For a scorer that good, that number was way too low, all because he was too slim to bully defenders and draw contact at the rim. But the timing of when he pulled this off is what makes it so impressive. Tatum barely had a summer to do any of this, since he spent most of it playing for Team USA and won a gold medal in Tokyo. So while everyone was hyping up the Giannis comparison, Tatum shrugged it off and said his body was just getting older and he was putting in the work. And that quiet transformation was the first real step toward him becoming the two-way superstar he is today.
